# 17 が作ったクラスタを、案内どおり1つ上げた位置で 18 に渡したらどうなるか（#485）
# 上流は image（docker-library/postgres）。container CLI 1.2.2 / 2026-08-23
# ビルドの同一性は、両方の実行の直前に出している opossum バイナリの shasum で読む
# 読み方は末尾の対照とあわせて：ここで案内が出ないのは、マウント位置が既に 18 の求める場所だから
$ shasum $(which opossum) | awk '{print $1}'
e8e648576c23cebb6f74110a849d56745cdb8ba9
$ container image inspect postgres:18-alpine | grep -m1 digest
        "digest" : "sha256:9a8afca54e7861fd90fab5fdf4c42477a6b1cb7d293595148e674e0a3181de15",
$ container run --rm --volume pg17-make_data17:/v alpine sh -c 'cat /v/PG_VERSION; ls /v | head -4'
17
PG_VERSION
base
global
pg_commit_ts
$ cat compose.yaml
services:
  s:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: x
    volumes:
      - pg17-make_data17:/var/lib/postgresql
volumes:
  pg17-make_data17:
    external: true
$ opossum up --no-supervisor
Creating network pg18-inherit-net
Starting s (postgres:18-alpine)
s.pg18-inherit.opossum
warning: [OPSM-407] service "s" exited right after starting (state "stopped"); its last log lines:
  format which is compatible with "pg_ctlcluster" (specifically, using
         major-version-specific directory names).  This better reflects how
         PostgreSQL itself works, and how upgrades are to be performed.
         See also https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/pull/1259
         Counter to that, there appears to be PostgreSQL data in:
           /var/lib/postgresql
         This is usually the result of upgrading the Docker image without
         upgrading the underlying database using "pg_upgrade" (which requires both
         versions).
         The suggested container configuration for 18+ is to place a single mount
         at /var/lib/postgresql which will then place PostgreSQL data in a
         subdirectory, allowing usage of "pg_upgrade --link" without mount point
         boundary issues.
         See https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/issues/37 for a (long)
         discussion around this process, and suggestions for how to do so.
opossum: [OPSM-407] 1 service(s) exited right after starting: "s" — see the logs above, fix the cause, and run `opossum up` again
$ opossum ps | tail -1   # 見出し行は落としている
s        s.pg18-inherit.opossum  postgres:18-alpine  -   -      stopped
$ container run --rm --volume pg17-make_data17:/v alpine sh -c 'ls -d /v/18/docker; ls -A /v/18/docker | wc -l; cat /v/PG_VERSION'
/v/18/docker
0
17

# --- 対照：同じバイナリ（上と同じ shasum）で、旧パスにマウントすると案内が出る ---
$ cd ../pg18
$ shasum $(which opossum) | awk '{print $1}'
e8e648576c23cebb6f74110a849d56745cdb8ba9
$ cat compose.yaml
services:
  s:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: x
    volumes:
      - ./data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
$ opossum up --no-supervisor
Creating network pg18-net
Starting s (postgres:18-alpine)
s.pg18.opossum
warning: [OPSM-407] service "s" exited right after starting (state "stopped"); its last log lines:
  format which is compatible with "pg_ctlcluster" (specifically, using
         major-version-specific directory names).  This better reflects how
         PostgreSQL itself works, and how upgrades are to be performed.
         See also https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/pull/1259
         Counter to that, there appears to be PostgreSQL data in:
           /var/lib/postgresql/data (unused mount/volume)
         This is usually the result of upgrading the Docker image without
         upgrading the underlying database using "pg_upgrade" (which requires both
         versions).
         The suggested container configuration for 18+ is to place a single mount
         at /var/lib/postgresql which will then place PostgreSQL data in a
         subdirectory, allowing usage of "pg_upgrade --link" without mount point
         boundary issues.
         See https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/issues/37 for a (long)
         discussion around this process, and suggestions for how to do so.
  → [OPSM-110] Postgres 18 and newer keep the cluster in a major-version subdirectory, so the mount belongs one level up: mount `/var/lib/postgresql` instead of `/var/lib/postgresql/data` (this service mounts ./data there). A host path works there — the image creates the subdirectory itself. Data an earlier major version wrote is a separate question: the image asks for `pg_upgrade`, which moving the mount does not do.
opossum: [OPSM-407] 1 service(s) exited right after starting: "s" — see the logs above, fix the cause, and run `opossum up` again
